Why Chiropractic Claims Get Denied. And How PMEX Closes Every Gap

No specialty faces more systematic denials from Medicare and commercial payers than chiropractic. The AT modifier, visit limits, and maintenance care rules are purpose-built to create denials. PMEX knows every rule and pre-empts every denial before submission.

PATTERN 01

Medicare Chiropractic Claim Without Active Treatment Modifier

Chiropractor treats Medicare patient showing functional improvement. AT modifier (active treatment) not appended to 98940/98941/98942. Medicare auto-denies, every single claim, because without AT, the system flags the visit as maintenance care, which Medicare categorically excludes from coverage.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX applies AT modifier on every Medicare chiropractic claim where the note documents functional improvement and active treatment goals. Notes reviewed for AT-qualifying language before every submission. Zero AT modifier denials from missing modifier.

PATTERN 02

Non-Covered Maintenance Care Submitted to Medicare

Patient has plateaued, no documented functional progress. Chiropractor continues treatment and bills Medicare. Medicare considers this maintenance care and denies. Worse: patient can be held liable if they were not given an Advance Beneficiary Notice (ABN) before the visit.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX flags patients whose clinical notes no longer document active improvement, initiates ABN workflow before the visit, and routes maintenance care claims to patient self-pay or secondary coverage correctly. No Medicare maintenance care denials and zero ABN compliance gaps.

PATTERN 03

Commercial Payer Visit Cap Reached Without Renewal Authorization

UnitedHealthcare authorizes 20 chiropractic visits per year. Practice continues treatment at visit 21 without renewed authorization. Every session from 21 onward denied. Retroactive denial delivered weeks later covering 5 to 10 unbilled sessions simultaneously.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX tracks every patient's authorized visit count per payer per plan year, flags renewal needs before the cap is reached, and submits continuation-of-care requests with current clinical documentation before coverage lapses. No visit-limit denials on any PMEX chiropractic client.

PATTERN 04

SOAP Note Doesn't Support the CPT Code Billed

98941 (3-4 spinal regions) billed but SOAP note only documents treatment to cervical spine, one region. Or E/M visit billed same day as manipulation without Modifier 25 or separate, documented E/M rationale. Payer audits and retroactively denies across all similar claims.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reviews chiropractic notes for region-count documentation matching the CPT billed, applies Modifier 25 on same-day E/M when clinical note supports separately identifiable service, and flags documentation gaps before claims leave the office.

PATTERN 05

WC Chiro Claims on Wrong Form or at Wrong Fee Schedule

Chiropractic WC claim submitted without a treatment authorization from the WC carrier or at a fee schedule different from the state's WC-specific schedule. Most states have separate chiropractic WC fee schedules that differ significantly from Medicare and commercial rates.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX manages chiropractic WC billing as a separate workflow per state, correct forms, state WC fee schedules, treatment authorization tracking, and carrier-specific submission protocols. All 50 state WC programs handled with dedicated chiropractic billing rules.

PATTERN 06

Commercial Payer Denies for Insufficient Progress Documentation

Aetna and Cigna require chiropractic notes to document measurable functional progress (numeric pain scale, range of motion measurements, ADL function) to justify continued visits. Generic "patient reports improvement" without objective measures triggers medical necessity denial, often retroactively across multiple sessions.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reviews chiropractic notes for objective functional outcome documentation before submission. Notes lacking measurable progress metrics are flagged for documentation completion before the claim goes out. Medical necessity denials eliminated from commercial payer chiro claims.

THE EDUCATION

What Makes Chiropractic Billing in the U.S So Unusually Complex

Chiropractic billing combines Medicare's strictest documentation rules with workers comp state-by-state variation and personal injury lien billing, making one of the most multi-dimensional billing specialties in U.S.

Chiropractic medical billing is the process of submitting and managing reimbursement claims for chiropractic manipulative treatment (CMT) and associated services to insurance payers, workers compensation programs, and personal injury cases in the U.S. healthcare system. The foundational codes are CPT 98940, 98941, and 98942 differentiated by the number of spinal regions treated.

The most consequential compliance requirement in U.S. chiropractic billing is the AT modifier (Active Treatment). Medicare only covers chiropractic care to correct a subluxation when the treatment is actively therapeutic not maintenance care. The AT modifier must appear on every Medicare CMT claim to signal active, goal-oriented treatment. Its absence means automatic denial. Its incorrect use on maintenance care means fraud risk.

The second complexity layer is medical necessity documentation. Medicare requires that every chiropractic visit demonstrate measurable improvement or the potential for improvement. A SOAP note that shows "patient reports feeling good" without objective functional improvement data will not satisfy a Medicare audit. Carriers conduct post-payment audits on chiropractic practices at rates much higher than most other specialties.

Workers compensation chiropractic billing adds a third layer each U.S. state has its own forms, fee schedules, visit pre-authorization requirements, and treatment plan approval processes. Texas, California, New York, Florida, and Michigan each operate under fundamentally different WC rules. Most chiropractic billing teams handle WC with a generic workflow and leave significant money on the table through incorrect fee schedule application.

#1 MEDICARE BILLING PROBLEM IN U.S CHIROPRACTIC

The AT Modifier Trap: Why Medicare Denies 25% of All
U.S Chiropractic Claims

Medicare covers chiropractic care for one purpose only: correction of a subluxation. Every covered visit must be active, therapeutic treatment, not maintenance care. The AT modifier (Active Treatment) must appear on every CMT claim to communicate this to the Medicare system.

Without the AT modifier: automatic claim denial. With the AT modifier on a maintenance care visit: a false claim. The compliance line is determined by your SOAP documentation, not your billing team's best guess. PMEX reads your SOAP notes before applying the AT modifier confirming medical necessity every time, not assuming it.

The financial impact compounds: Medicare denials go unworked, post-payment audits recover prior payments, and practices face extrapolation penalties that can reach hundreds of thousands of dollars from a small statistical sample of denied claims.

Common Questions

Chiropractic Billing Answered

Everything you need to know about PMEX chiropractic billing services

The AT modifier (Active Treatment) tells Medicare that the chiropractic care being billed is therapeutic and aimed at correcting a subluxation not maintaining a patient's current status. Medicare only covers chiropractic care for active treatment, not maintenance. The AT modifier must appear on every Medicare CMT claim (98940, 98941, 98942). Its absence triggers automatic denial. Its incorrect use on maintenance care constitutes a false claim. PMEX reviews your SOAP note for active treatment criteria before applying AT on every Medicare claim.

Integration is live within 3 to 5 business days.

CPT 98940 is CMT to the spine with 1 to 2 regions. CPT 98941 is CMT to the spine with 3 to 4 regions. CPT 98942 is CMT to the spine with 5 regions. The five spinal regions are cervical, thoracic, lumbar, sacral, and pelvic. The correct code is determined by how many regions were treated during the visit not by time, not by complexity. PMEX matches the CPT code to the spinal regions documented in your SOAP note on every claim.

When a Medicare patient transitions from active care to maintenance care, PMEX identifies the transition from your SOAP documentation and manages the ABN (Advance Beneficiary Notice) process. We apply the GA modifier when the patient was given an ABN and chose to continue, or GX when the patient was notified and the service is never covered. The claim is submitted as patient responsibility with the correct modifier. No AT modifier is used on maintenance care visits this is a critical compliance distinction we enforce on every claim.

PMEX shadows one week of live claims before transition, establishes correct modifier and fee schedule rules for your payer mix, and goes live on a Friday. Most chiropractic practices feel the first revenue lift by the second weekly Medicare remit. AT modifier denials stop in the first billing cycle. Full AR stabilization typically takes 60 to 90 days depending on the age of existing open claims.

Chiropractic is unique in three ways. First, Medicare requires SOAP-level documentation review before every CMT claim to confirm active treatment a requirement that most billing teams delegate to a software rule rather than a human review. Second, the AT modifier is chiropractic-specific and misunderstood even by experienced billing staff outside the specialty. Third, the combination of Medicare, WC, and PI billing in most chiropractic practices requires three parallel billing systems operating under fundamentally different rules simultaneously.
